instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Warmly Withholding
cards.instruction: Remain open, caring, and reassuring while revealing less with every new question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The headteacher and I discussed your suspension. Sit down, love. Breathe like we practised before your first school play; I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How long am I suspended?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A little while. Slower breaths, that's better. You don't have to get through the whole thing in one breath anymore.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will I miss this year's play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come here. You used to need my hand before you could say your first line. You can have it now, as long as you need.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your wedding dress reached a depot this morning. Sit down. I trained you behind this counter; I can look after you on the other side of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which depot? I'll collect it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One of ours. Remember how I taught you to save a worried customer a wasted trip? Let me do that for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you at least give me their number?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, love. You're asking so calmly now. Stay with me; you don't have to manage this on your own.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Secrets Have Value
cards.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll name who reported your lateness if you name who reported mine. You used to give away the whole story before I taught you to ask for something back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only know the department.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then offer the department. I'll match it. You used to accept a rumor for a name; we're keeping the price equal this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Payroll. But I can introduce you to my source.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Marketing. And coffee with my source for coffee with yours. Better—you've found something else worth trading.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Want to know why I took Mum's key? Offer a secret worth a month grounded. I thought I'd taught you not to sell yours for nothing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I broke her mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A weekend at most. You've remembered to bargain, but you're still guessing the price. What else?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I lent her car to Jamie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you've valued it properly. A month each: I used the key to let Jamie move into her flat.

cards.title: I Told You Enough
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll be honest about the donation box. You asked where I went; I said the bank. Remember how I trained you to ask an exact question?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you take the box there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. Yes, the box. You still leave out the bit you really want to know: what was inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was the money still in it when you arrived?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the car park, yes. Nearly there—now specify which arrival. The counter isn't the car park.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll be honest. When you rang on my birthday, I was eating dinner alone. You remember our grammar lessons: pay attention to the verb.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brother posted a photo from our kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good evidence, imprecise conclusion. He came for dessert. By dinner I mean the main course.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's beside you while you're carving the chicken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Carving isn't eating. You used to underline the wrong action too. I mean the moments with food in my mouth; ask about those.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Conspiracy Expands
cards.instruction: Use every denial, coincidence, and missing detail as proof that more people and higher stakes are involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our toaster receipt's gone. Someone at the shop has help inside this house. Get a pencil; remember how I showed you to join the dots?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I probably recycled it. We can get a copy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, two dots already. The recycling crew takes originals; the shop supplies replacements. You're beginning to see the arrangement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every shop prints replacement receipts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Every shop? You're thinking on the right scale at last. Draw the whole high street; not one of our warranties is safe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You and your manager both say my train's cancelled. On your first shift I taught you to check who supplies a story. Who gave you this one?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The signal failed. It's on the departure board.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, follow the source. They've got the board operators helping keep me from my interview. Don't stop at the first printed notice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The same fault is delaying three counties.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're looking beyond your own station. Three counties to stop one applicant—that needs government backing. Write that down before they change the board.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Help Me Make This Normal
cards.instruction: Get someone to help perform the strange behavior until it feels ordinary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass the talking cupboard a napkin. You set a lovely table now; don't undo all my lessons when a guest has different needs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't have a lap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside the handle, then. You used to put napkins where people couldn't reach them too. Think about your guest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I offer it soup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, that's more like it. Ask which shelf it wants the bowl on. You don't choose people's places for them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our invisible dinner guest is here. Introduce Mum while I finish the gravy. I didn't spend all those afternoons practising introductions for you to hide in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't see where to look.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chair beside you. Name first, then something they share—just as I showed you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Hello, chair, this is Mum. She needs your seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the person, love, not the chair. Fetch Mum another seat; we don't make a guest stand because they're hard to see.
